name: AI Chat
description: A chat with a small language model that downloads once and runs entirely in your browser; nothing you type leaves the machine

name: Device Kit
description: A tour of what a sandboxed app may ask for: fetch a URL, read and make QR codes, take a photo, open a file — each behind the permission that gates it

name: Glamour Studio
description: A salon's front desk: appointments, clients, staff and services in a local-first database that syncs between devices

name: GPU Compute
description: Vector maths on your graphics card: two compute shaders run through the runtime's WebGPU bridge, with the numbers shown as they come back

name: Maze Escape 3D
description: A first-person maze carved fresh every game: find the golden ring, with a minimap that fills in as you explore and a best time that sticks

name: Notes
description: A shared notes board kept in the app's own storage on this site: add, search and delete, and everyone who opens it here sees the same notes

name: Pocket
description: An 8-bit handheld emulator — CPU, PPU, APU and mappers all in .logic, drawn by PixelCanvas and heard through AudioStream

name: SoftDOS
description: An x86 PC emulator written in .logic: a 16/32-bit CPU with the full 386 integer instruction set, VGA mode 13h and 80x25 text, a BIOS and DOS kernel, and a command line that runs real 8086 programs.

name: Component Showcase
description: Every chart, animation and interactive component the runtime ships, on three pages, in light and dark

name: Snake
description: The classic: eat, grow, don't hit the walls — with a shared top ten kept on the site

name: Texas Hold'em
description: Multiplayer Texas Hold'em Poker with P2P sync

name: TheOffice
description: Local AI sim game where 6 Office-inspired characters chat autonomously using Qwen3.5-0.8B

name: 3D Scene
description: Seven shapes drifting over a floor: drag to look around, click a shape to select it, add more and recolour them

name: WarbleWire
description: Send a message as synthetic birdsong and decode it back — the QXW acoustic transport

name: Promptly Unemployed
description: First-person 3D narrative tragicomedy, part one: laid off by an avatar, home by dinner, a business by midnight. Fully voiced, and one file.

name: Blockscape
description: A first-person voxel sandbox: an island of blocks to mine, build on and save, with gravity, swimming, flight and a day-night cycle

name: Dead Hours
description: A first-person zombie shooter: hold a fenced yard at night against waves of the dead with a pistol and a shotgun
The sliding-tile classic: merge equal tiles to reach 2048 and beyond, with undo and a best score

name: Blockfall
description: Falling blocks in a 10×20 well: seven pieces, wall kicks, a ghost piece, hold, a preview, and levels that speed up

name: Model Train Yard
description: An animated HO-scale model train yard diorama on a wooden table with running trains, turntable, busy harbor, town, day-night cycle, and tactile physical controls

name: Predator-Prey Simulator
description: An interactive 3D ecosystem diorama: watch foxes hunt rabbits, rabbits graze on grass, and population dynamics balance in real time

name: House Builder
description: Draw a house from above and see it in 3D: walls, doors, windows, room floors, a roof, furniture and garden, then walk through it in first person

name: Sim Lives
description: Build a house, design avatars and move a household in: steer them to eat, sleep, wash, play and chat, or switch on free will and watch their day
